links.claim: NKRF is the leading binding candidate in this chain because its own QBiC-SELEX model predicts stronger binding to ref G at a strong site. A variant-overlapping NKRF ChIP peak exists in GM12878, but no matching glioblastoma peak is reported, so NKRF occupancy in glioblastoma is unconfirmed.
The variant is annotated within ENSR5_C5GP, but it overlaps no ENCODE cCRE; the nearest pELS is 75 bp away, so the functional element assignment is uncertain.
TERT is the nearest listed gene and is named among the nearby cCRE genes, but no supplied evidence demonstrates that this variant or element regulates TERT; no significant GTEx eQTL is reported.
Glioblastoma is a candidate context because NKRF is expressed in the DepMap glioblastoma subtype, but the supplied evidence does not establish NKRF occupancy or regulatory activity there.

TERT has general relevance to melanoma and glioblastoma in the cited literature, but no evidence here connects rs34768248 to either disease; no bladder-cancer connection for this variant is established.

predictions: If NKRF occupies the site in relevant tumor cells, allele-specific occupancy should favor G over A; this differs from H3, which predicts an A-favoring CREB1 effect.

If the variant has a local regulatory consequence through this chain, perturbing the base should produce an NKRF-dependent regulatory change; the direction of TERT expression cannot be inferred from binding direction alone.
falsified_if: A sensitive relevant-cell assay detects no NKRF occupancy at the variant, or detects occupancy without the predicted G-over-A difference.
Editing the variant produces no reproducible NKRF-dependent local regulatory effect.

A major molecular feature of melanoma is abnormal telomerase activation; this is most often caused by telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter mutations, which occur in 50-82% of cases and are the most common noncoding alteration in this cancer.

Conclusions: Understanding both telomere-dependent and -independent TERT functions is essential for developing effective biomarkers and therapies that overcome resistance and slow melanoma progression.
The genetic landscape of familial melanoma is heterogeneous.
CDKN2A and CDK4 mutations act through UV-dependent and cell cycle disruption pathways, while BAP1, POT1, and TERT mutations are considered UV-independent.
BackgroundMutations in the telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter region (TPM), particularly C228T and C250T, are common in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (GBM).

ConclusionThe rs2853669 C allele may increase GBM susceptibility and, when in cis with TPM, is associated with reduced TERT expression and poorer prognosis, underscoring its biological and clinical significance in TPM-mutant GBM.
Additionally, loss of either USP10 or FOXM1 suppresses the expression of the downstream target Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), triggering cellular senescence.

TERT promoter (TERTp) mutations are among the most frequent molecular alterations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type glioblastoma (GBM), yet the molecular profiles and prognostic implications associated with TERTp status remain incompletely characterized.
The prognostic relevance of CDKN2A deletion may vary according to TERTp status, particularly for OS.
